extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer review researchers, methodologists and policymakers interested in the evidence on peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the metrics, criteria and outcome measures used in studies of journal peer review — including instruments for rating reviewer reports, manuscript quality, timeliness, bias, and the impact of interventions (training, blinding, statistical review, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussed importance of the research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer discuss the importance of the research question?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of an 8‑item quality instrument (grading 1 = not at all to 5 = discussed extensively). Used to judge whether reviewers address the paper's central question and its relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussed originality of the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer discuss the originality of the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 8‑item quality instrument item. Assesses whether the reviewers comment on novelty and contribution to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identified strengths and weaknesses of the methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer clearly identify the strengths and weaknesses of the method (study design, data collection and data analysis)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 8‑item instrument item. Focus on methodological critique (design, data collection, analysis). Critical for assessing methodological rigour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific useful comments on writing, organisation, tables and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer make specific useful comments on the writing, organisation, tables and figures of the manuscript?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 8‑item instrument item. Emphasises constructive, actionable feedback on presentation and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructiveness of reviewer's comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Were the reviewer's comments constructive?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 8‑item instrument item. Evaluates tone and whether comments help authors improve the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evidence/examples from the paper to substantiate comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer supply appropriate evidence using examples from the paper to substantiate their comments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 8‑item instrument item. Measures whether criticisms are supported by specific examples rather than vague assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on author's interpretation of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer comment on the author's interpretation of the results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 8‑item instrument item. Checks whether reviewer assesses if conclusions are justified by the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall quality of the review (global rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: How would you rate the quality of this review overall?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 8‑item instrument item and general global rating (e.g., 1–5). Used as a summary judgement of review usefulness and thoroughness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy: hypothesis / purpose / theoretic model
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification category for reviewer comments addressing hypothesis, purpose and theoretical model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of eight categories in a 99‑item checklist used to classify review comments (Day 2002). Useful to quantify emphasis on conceptual issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy: study design / power
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification category for reviewer comments on study design and statistical power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of eight categories in a 99‑item checklist. Captures critique about adequacy of design and sample size/power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy: research and analytic methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification category for reviewer comments on research and analytic (non‑statistical) methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of eight categories in a 99‑item checklist. Encompasses data collection, measurement, protocol issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy: statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification category for reviewer comments on statistical methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of eight categories in a 99‑item checklist. Used to capture statistical critique distinct from general analytic methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy: presentation of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification category for reviewer comments on how methods are presented in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of eight categories in a 99‑item checklist. Assesses clarity and completeness of method reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy: presentation of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification category for reviewer comments on presentation of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of eight categories in a 99‑item checklist. Includes clarity of tables, figures, reported statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy: interpretation of results / limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification category for reviewer comments on interpretation of results and limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of eight categories in a 99‑item checklist. Evaluates whether reviewers address over‑interpretation, confounding, and caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy: other comments (non‑methodology/statistical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Catch‑all category for reviewer comments not related to methodology/statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of eight categories in a 99‑item checklist (e.g., clinical relevance, editorial matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Goodman scale: manuscript quality (modified 9‑point / section scores 0–10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of final manuscript compared to its original version assessed using a modified version of the Goodman scale (originally 9‑point; modification used section scoring 0–10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare original and final manuscripts; modification noted because of poor inter‑rater agreement and cultural factors. Scored by blinded statisticians in one trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript quality (34‑item scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of manuscript assessed on a 34‑item scale and rated by 'expert' assessors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to judge improvements after peer review and editing; detailed multi‑item instrument to capture reporting quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mean number of weaknesses detected by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Mean number of weaknesses or defects in a manuscript detected by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome used in trials (e.g., Godlee 1998) to measure reviewer thoroughness and sensitivity to flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality (7‑item editor‑rated scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of review assessed on a 7‑item scale by editors (items vary by study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Widely used summary instrument in multiple trials; used to compare interventions (blinding, signing, training). Specific item content sometimes unspecified in summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to review / editorial turnaround time
rubrics_metrics.description: Time (days) from manuscript mailing/enrolment to reception of review or total editorial turnaround time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common process metric: used to compare interventions (e.g., telephoning reviewers, 'askfirst' vs 'justsend') and to assess timeliness trade‑offs of policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of readers' comments (post‑publication electronic commenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of readers' comments received after posting reviews or manuscripts online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an engagement/outreach outcome (e.g., impact of publishing reviewers' comments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript revisions (number/extent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent or number of revisions made to a manuscript in response to peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome indicating reviewer impact on manuscript improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer's recommendation (accept / reject / revise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer’s recommendation regarding acceptance or publication suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard outcome used to study effects of interventions (training, blinding) on decision recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congruence with editors' decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which reviewers' recommendations align with editors' final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to study reviewer‑editor agreement and the predictive value of review recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter‑rater agreement / reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of agreement (e.g., kappa, inter‑rater correlation) between assessors or reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an important quality property of rating instruments; often low in peer review studies (e.g., kappa = 0.32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of deliberate major and minor errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of deliberately inserted major and minor errors identified by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in training and testing trials (e.g., Schroter) as an objective measure of reviewers' ability to spot substantive flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of papers considered statistically acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of submissions judged statistically acceptable upon submission and after review/publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure the effect of statistical review and checklists on the statistical quality of published studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of statistical referee and checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a dedicated statistical/methodology reviewer and structured checklists to assess manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process/intervention metric; studies report that statistical referees using checklists emphasise methodological issues and can improve statistical quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling techniques reported (validity criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether studies report and use appropriate sampling techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the validity criteria used to assess published studies' methodological quality (Elvik).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total and mean sample size reported (validity criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting of total and mean sample sizes in the studied papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validity criterion for assessing methodological quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of accident or injury severity (validity criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the study specifies accident or injury severity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific validity criterion used in road safety evaluations; example of domain‑specific reporting items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate study design (validity criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of an appropriate study design for the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core validity item used when comparing journals with and without peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of confounding factors controlled (validity criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: How many potential confounding factors were identified and controlled for in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of methodological validity assessment; more controlled confounders increases internal validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of moderator variables specified (validity criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: How many moderator (interaction) variables are specified in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an index of reporting completeness and analytical depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barnes and Bero 12‑point tool for review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: A 12‑point questionnaire (e.g., evaluating inclusion criteria on a 3‑point scale: 0=no; 1=partial; 2=yes) to evaluate methodological quality of review articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess methodological quality of review articles in comparative studies of peer‑reviewed vs throwaway journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation features (tables, figures, photographs, colour, font size)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of presentation elements such as number of tables, figures, photographs, use of colour and font sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation/readability outcome reflecting appeal to readers; throwaway journals scored higher on presentation features in one study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability indices (Flesch and Gunning FOG scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Readability assessed using Flesch index score and Gunning FOG index score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective readability metrics used to compare articles' accessibility to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical relevance / usefulness for practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer/reader ratings (e.g., 5‑point scales) on whether the article provides useful information for clinical practice and would be read/used by clinicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed by recently qualified physicians using statements about importance, relevance, and usefulness for practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of peer review on manuscript content and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether peer review improved content, organisation, clarity of conclusions, changed conclusions, or improved statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome set used to quantify the substantive impact of peer review on manuscripts (authors' perceptions or rated by external assessors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion agreeing to review / opt‑out and decline rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of invited reviewers who agree to review versus those who decline or do not respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational metric affecting feasibility; compared across policies (e.g., 'askfirst' increased initial declines but faster turnaround for those who agreed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer productivity: number and mean rating of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of reviews completed by a reviewer and mean quality rating (e.g., average review quality score over time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess change in reviewer activity and performance after interventions such as training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer bias toward orthodox/conventional interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency of reviewers to favor conventional/orthodox interventions over unconventional ones, independent of methodological quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detected by sending near‑identical manuscripts that vary only by intervention type; significant bias against unconventional treatments has been observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of blinding / revealing reviewer and author identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect on review quality, recommendations and time when reviewers/authors/co‑reviewer identities are masked or revealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple trials: blinding often had no consistent effect on quality, while signing reviews may increase thoroughness but also time taken; evidence mixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of review as judged by authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors' rating of the quality and usefulness of reviewer reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside editor ratings to capture recipient perspective on review helpfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of submissions accepted for publication (journal acceptance rate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an outcome to study effects of guidelines, training, or peer review policies on editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of reviewer/editor guidelines for managing submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether introduction of guidelines for review and revision helps editors manage submissions and affects submission quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed to help editors' workflow (e.g., economic submissions guidelines) though not necessarily to change manuscript quality in the short term.
